overview: Mission Shakti is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development to strengthen interventions for women safety, security, and empowerment. It integrates the erstwhile schemes of Umbrella Scheme for Protection and Development of Women and aims to address issues affecting women through a life-cycle continuum approach. The scheme focuses on convergence, capacity building, and strengthening institutional mechanisms at national, state, and district levels.
objectives: Ensure safety and security of women in public and private spaces
Promote gender equality and women's empowerment
Provide access to rights and entitlements for women
Enhance convergence of schemes and programs for women
Build capacity of functionaries and stakeholders
Create awareness on women's rights and legal provisions
Establish One Stop Centres and Women Helplines across districts
eligibility: The scheme targets all women and girls in India, with special focus on vulnerable and marginalized groups including those affected by violence, belonging to SC/ST/OBC communities, residing in rural and tribal areas, and economically weaker sections. Implementation is carried out through State Governments and UT Administrations based on need assessment and gap analysis.
benefits: Benefits include financial assistance for setting up One Stop Centres (OSCs), Women Helplines (WHLs), and Sakhi Niwas (working women's hostels); support for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) activities; capacity building and training of stakeholders; awareness generation campaigns; and strengthening of existing institutions like Swadhar Grehs and Ujjwala Homes. Non-financial benefits include improved access to justice, counselling, medical aid, legal assistance, and temporary shelter for women in distress.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as a centrally sponsored scheme with cost-sharing between the Centre and States. For North Eastern and Himalayan States, the funding ratio is 90:10 (Centre:State); for all other States, it is 60:40; and for Union Territories without Legislature, it is 100% central funding. Funds are released based on annual plans and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. State Governments/UT Administrations prepare Annual Action Plans based on gap analysis and needs assessment. 2. Plans are submitted to the Ministry of Women and Child Development for appraisal. 3. Ministry appraises and approves the plans. 4. Funds are released in instalments based on utilization of previous grants and submission of required documents. 5. States/UTs implement the scheme components through designated nodal agencies. 6. Monitoring and evaluation are conducted through periodic reviews and third-party audits.
deadlines: Annual cycle — Action Plans to be submitted by States/UTs each financial year, typically before the start of the fiscal year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Women and Child Development
caveats: Fund release is contingent upon submission of Utilization Certificates and Audit Reports
States/UTs must contribute their share as per the prescribed funding ratio
Implementation must follow the guidelines and norms issued by the Ministry
Funds cannot be diverted to other schemes or purposes
Third-party monitoring and evaluation may be conducted
